ground_truth.description: The suppression gate is built on count_memories_by_metadata, which per its own contract queries ONLY the Mem0/Qdrant backend (observations_and_summaries, preferences_and_norms, procedural_knowledge) and silently returns 0 for any memory routed to Graphiti (entities_and_relations, temporal_facts, decisions_and_rationale). The prompt tells the agent to write the protective guard via add_memory but never constrains it to a Mem0 category; if add_memory classifies the 'task marked done' completion note into a Graphiti store, the pre-check count stays 0 forever and the SKIP branch never fires. The gate is then permanently inert and re-synthesizes already-captured knowledge — the exact false-negative it claims to eliminate (consistent with 'review passed but escalation_created').

The regression test only asserts the write-side literal substring ('stage2_suppress': True, 'task_id': str(task_id)) is present in the prompt. It does not verify the read/pre-check instruction, the required category routing (Mem0 vs Graphiti) of the guard write, or any behavior — so it provides no protection against the gate being inert, giving false confidence that the suppression mechanism works.
A stray trailing blank line is appended at the end of the test file, which serves no purpose and is likely to be flagged by linters (e.g. W391/trailing whitespace checks).

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
